title: Causal Representation Learning for Generalisable Recommendation
abstract: arXiv:2605.27043v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Predictive models trained on observational data often fail to generalise when deployed, especially when the training data is a product of the system being optimised. Recommender systems are a canonical example: they are trained on interaction logs confounded by the deployed policy, past user behaviour, and platform filtering. As a result, the training distribution differs from the candidate distribution scored at serving time, a gap that makes offline metrics unreliable predictors of online performance. We address the distribution shift problem with a method motivated by causal representation learning (CRL). We propose an information-theoretic disentanglement criterion and prove that its optimum excludes confounder-dependent non-causal information from the treatment representation. translated_title: 面向可泛化推荐的因果表征学习
translated_abstract: 在观测数据上训练的预测模型在部署时往往难以泛化，尤其是当训练数据本身是被优化系统运行所产生的结果时。推荐系统就是一个典型的例子：它们是在交互日志上进行训练的，而这些日志受到已部署策略、用户历史行为以及平台过滤机制的混淆。其结果是，训练分布与服务阶段所评分的候选分布并不一致，这一差距使得离线指标无法可靠地预测线上表现。我们提出一种受因果表征学习（CRL）启发的方法来解决该分布偏移问题。我们提出了一种信息论解耦准则，并证明其最优解能够从处理（treatment）表征中排除依赖于混淆因子的非因果信息。我们进一步推导出一个可计算的变分下界，使该准则能够基于有限的观测数据进行优化。我们方法的适用范围比……
tldr: 该论文提出一种基于因果表征学习的推荐方法，通过信息论解耦准则和可优化的变分下界，从处理表征中剔除受混淆因子影响的非因果信息，从而解决训练分布与服务分布不一致导致的推荐模型泛化难题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a causal representation learning method for recommendation that employs an information-theoretic disentanglement criterion with a tractable variational lower bound to exclude confounder-dependent non-causal information from treatment representations, addressing the distribution shift between training and serving that undermines model generalisation.
